## For teachers

These additional cases record supported behavior, invalid or unsupported
inputs, and known differences found while developing STACK SymPy. They are
separate from the [2,303 imported STACK cases](index.qmd).

### How to use the cases

**Expected** is the intended result for the case. **Port** is this SymPy
implementation, **STACK** is Maxima, and **Browser** runs the port through
Pyodide. Amber cases explain what differs and what it means for a question.
Browser agreement may reproduce the same known issue; it does not make that
result mathematically correct.

For teaching, state the domain, select the intended written form and use a
numerical test for approximate answers. The [semantics reference for STACK authors](semantics.qmd#author-attention) discusses unresolved conventions in detail. The
[authoring guide](../docs/authoring.html) explains supported features and how
to test your own questions, including [matrix conditions and SPD](../docs/python-checker-api.html).

<div class="status-legend" aria-label="How to read the colors">
  <span class="tone-good">Green: expected behavior or agreement</span>
  <span class="tone-notice">Amber: known issue or explained difference</span>
  <span class="tone-bad">Red: unexpected result</span>
  <span class="tone-neutral">Gray: input handling or no comparison</span>
</div>

## For developers

### Scope and interpretation

An input-handling check verifies that invalid or unsupported input is refused;
it is not a successful mathematical comparison. Known port issues remain
issues when their observations match an expected exception. Root-convention
differences have their own explanation rather than a mathematical-failure label.

The saved run observes isolated Python, official STACK functions where
applicable, and the same port in browser Pyodide. “Test applies” describes
answer-test applicability, separately from syntax validity. Missing observations
remain unavailable. These regression counts do not alter the native inventory.

### Saved evidence and contribution

The [conventions reference](semantics.qmd) explains the case-specific
mathematics. Add focused project discoveries to the
[regression cases and contribution guide](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-sympy/tree/main/tests/port_regressions).
The [development guide](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-sympy#supported-subset-and-grading-behavior)
provides reproduction commands. Rendering this page reads saved results without
rerunning the mathematical checks.
